jobs.problemDescription: DOCK / Equipment Lifting / Tuggers / Other - Click NEXT and describe what is broken in Problem Description / Inspect 28 tugger carts.
jobs.resolution: Work Summary: Tugger Cart PM Inspection Summary Date: July 21–23, 2026 Location: FedEx – 696 E. Trimble Rd., San Jose, CA Technician: Dennis Bell-White  Over the course of three days, preventive maintenance inspections were completed on the FedEx tugger cart. Each cart received a thorough visual inspection of the frame, cargo deck, tow tongue, wheel assemblies, maneuver handle, cargo restraint system, and towing components.  Overall, the fleet was found to be in good structural condition. No cracked welds or major frame failures were identified. Most maintenance items were routine in nature and centered on normal wear from daily service.  The most common deficiencies identified included:  * Torn, damaged, or missing cargo restraint webbing/netting requiring replacement. * Missing safety chains, chain hooks, or both on front tow hitches. * Missing rear D-rings requiring welding to restore safe towing capability. * Worn or damaged front wheels requiring replacement. * Bent or damaged upper corner uprights requiring straightening or replacement. * Routine lubrication recommended for all wheel bearings, pivot points, and tow hitch assemblies.  Overall, the tugger cart remains serviceable. The recommended repairs are primarily preventative and intended to improve operator safety, ensure proper cargo restraint, and maintain safe towing operations. Completing these repairs will return the carts to optimal operating condition and extend their service life.  Submitted by: Dennis Bell-White Field Service Technician

jobs.problemDescription: DOCK / Equipment Lifting / Tuggers / Other - Click NEXT and describe what is broken in Problem Description / Inspect 11 tugger carts.
jobs.resolution: A visual inspection was completed on Tugger Carts #1 through #7 and #9 through #11 located at FedEx Ground, 1400 Business Center Dr., San Leandro, CA 94577. All inspected carts were found to be structurally sound and operational. No cracked welds, structural failures, or conditions requiring immediate removal from service were observed. All undercarriages, wheel assemblies, hitch assemblies, and safety chains were inspected and found to be in good operating condition.  The primary maintenance items identified throughout the fleet consist of cosmetic deterioration, including chipped paint and varying degrees of surface rust, along with several missing or damaged pull handles. To improve fleet appearance, corrosion resistance, and long-term service life, it is recommended that all carts exhibiting moderate to heavy surface rust be properly cleaned, prepared, and repainted Safety Yellow.  It is further recommended that all carts missing pull (pole) handles have new handles installed and that the bent handle identified during this inspection be replaced. These repairs will improve safe manual maneuverability whenever carts are disconnected from a tugger.  Two carts were observed without side cargo webbing/rail assemblies. Based on their current use as flat trailers, no recommendation is made to install side webbing or railing unless their intended application changes.  As part of the next scheduled preventive maintenance service, all lubrication points should be greased, surface corrosion should be treated as necessary, and routine inspections should continue. Based on this inspection, all inspected tugger carts are suitable for continued service.

jobs.problemDescription: OUTSIDE / Gate / Motorized Gate / Will not open (if gate failure impedes operational demands) / **************POSSIBLE RECALL****************** The store reported that the main metal building access gate (Gate #1) is stuck in the open position. The gate is automatic and normally opens and closes, but it is currently unable to close, creating a security issue for the store tonight. Store hours are 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Store # is fine. Emergency service has been requested. *********************************************** OUTSIDE / Gate / Motorized Gate "Equip:" Gate, Sliding, Powered "Tag ID"SFOA-EA1-BF001, "Brand" Unknown / Other - Click NEXT and describe what is broken in Problem Description / Main Gate- #1- Not working properly- Stays open- Needs to be reset- works for a couple hours and then stays open again- Please contact Shannon for further details: 415-716-3589. Thank you. / POSSIBLE RECALL FROM TN #354728706
jobs.resolution: First emergency visit: found damage done to motor and gear caused by bag in the gears of the motor. See previous WO w/ attached photo. Gate was operating after visit. Second emergency visit: Found loose connections to the exit loop circuit. Wiring was reterminated, tightened, and tested. Gate was operating after visit. Third emergency visit: Gate was operating through ~20 cycles then failed. Found that the bearings to the motor were failing causing gate to fail. Found that limit switch settings were reset due to failed gate and needed to be reprogrammed. During final inspection of the gate, we found that the edge sensor was nonexistent. Edge sensor needs to be ordered in order for the gate to fully operate properly. Frontline recommends purchasing and installing a new edge sensor. We also recommend replacing the failing motor due to repetitive damage to gears.
